Type

visuals.title: Where it presents
visuals.text: Painless haematuria is the signature; advanced disease gives a pelvic mass, and obstruction can damage the kidneys.

nodes: CT urogram: upper tract and staging

visuals.title: Field change: the whole urothelium
visuals.text: Renal pelvis, ureters, bladder and urethra are all exposed to carcinogens in urine, so the CT urogram images the whole tract.

glossary.Malignancy: A cancer: cells growing uncontrollably and able to invade or spread.
glossary.Transitional cells: Stretchy lining cells of the urinary tract that change shape as the bladder fills.
glossary.SCC: Squamous cell carcinoma, a cancer of flat squamous cells.
glossary.High-grade: Cancer cells that look very abnormal and tend to behave aggressively.
glossary.Superficial: Confined to the surface lining, not invading deeper muscle.
glossary.Occupational: Related to a person's job or workplace exposure.
glossary.Catheterisation: Passing a tube into the bladder to drain urine.
glossary.Macroscopic: Visible to the naked eye; visible haematuria.
glossary.Urinalysis: Testing urine, usually with a dipstick, for blood, protein, glucose and infection.
glossary.Urine microscopy: Looking at urine under a microscope for red cells, white cells, casts and organisms.
glossary.Frequency: Needing to pass urine more often than usual.
glossary.Dysuria: Pain or burning when passing urine.
glossary.Urgency: A sudden, hard-to-delay need to pass urine.
glossary.Pelvic mass: A lump felt in the lower abdomen or on pelvic examination.
glossary.Prognostic factor: Something that predicts how a disease is likely to turn out.
glossary.Metastasis: Spread of cancer from where it started to distant sites.
glossary.Renal failure: Loss of the kidneys' ability to filter blood and make urine.
glossary.Biopsy: Removal of a small piece of tissue for examination under the microscope.
glossary.Sensitive: Good at picking up the disease when it is there, so few cases are missed.
glossary.WCC: White cell count; a raised count can suggest infection or inflammation.
glossary.Upper urinary tract: The kidneys, renal pelvis and ureters.
glossary.Staging: Working out how far a cancer has spread, which guides treatment.
glossary.Adjuvant: Extra treatment given after the main treatment to reduce the chance of recurrence.
glossary.Intravesical chemotherapy: Chemotherapy instilled directly into the bladder through a catheter.
glossary.Immunotherapy: Treatment that stimulates the immune system to attack cancer cells.
glossary.Radiotherapy: Treatment using high-energy radiation to kill cancer cells.
glossary.Chemotherapy: Drugs that kill rapidly dividing cancer cells.
glossary.Systemic: Acting throughout the whole body rather than at one site.
glossary.Metabolites: Substances the body produces when it breaks down a chemical or drug.
glossary.Chronic inflammation: Long-lasting inflammation that can damage tissue and drive abnormal cell change.
glossary.Metaplasia: Replacement of one mature cell type by another, often in response to irritation.
glossary.Mucosa: The inner lining layer of a hollow organ such as the bladder.
glossary.Submucosa: The connective tissue layer just under the mucosa, above the muscle.
glossary.Bladder-preserving: Treatment that removes the cancer but keeps the bladder.
glossary.Renal pelvis: The funnel-shaped part of the kidney that collects urine and drains into the ureter.
glossary.Ureters: The tubes carrying urine from each kidney to the bladder.
glossary.Urethra: The tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body.
glossary.Rubber industry: Workplace where aromatic amine exposure historically raised bladder cancer risk.
